proposed_answer:
Use a one-time helper in the setup chunk, with a shared preferred extension, and use it in image chunks:
preferred_graphics_ext <- "svg"
include_preferred_graphics <- function(path, ext = preferred_graphics_ext) {
  candidate <- sub("[.][^./]+$", sprintf(".%s", ext), path)
  use <- file.exists(candidate)
  path[use] <- candidate[use]
  knitr::include_graphics(path, auto_pdf = FALSE)
}
# Later, in the image chunk:
include_preferred_graphics("external_figure.jpg")
Change the shared extension to "emf" when that is the desired available variant, or back to the raster extension for raster output. The helper is scoped to local paths with an existing extension, as in the supplied example; if the alternate file is absent it retains the supplied file. Its replacement-and-existence-check logic is derived from the displayed include_graphics auto_pdf branch. Existing calls written as knitr::include_graphics(...) must call include_preferred_graphics(...) to use this setting; merely defining the helper will not intercept namespace-qualified calls. The built-in auto_pdf applies to PDF alternatives for LaTeX output, and the dev/fig.ext device settings do not provide the requested external-path replacement. Pandoc's default-image-extension only handles extensionless paths, so it does not change external_figure.jpg.
